html:
The Federal Charter of 1291 is an alliance of the three valley communities of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden, sworn in early August 1291. Switzerland counts it as its founding.

The valleys controlled the approach to the Gotthard pass and wanted to keep their own judges and customs against the Habsburgs. They promised to help each other against any attack and to settle their disputes among themselves.

Other towns and valleys joined over the next two centuries, among them Lucerne, Zurich and Bern, forming the Old Swiss Confederacy. The charter was little known until the 1800s, when it was chosen as the birth certificate of the nation. Since 1891, 1 August has been the Swiss national day. The legend of William Tell belongs to the same story, and so does the victory at Morgarten.
